classification.difficultyReason: Expand beginning-of-year contributions as a geometric series, then use the supplied models to calculate interest and rearrange for a contribution.

content.prompt: Finster and Finster Superannuation offer a superannuation scheme with annual contributions of $\$12\,000$ invested at an interest rate of 9% p.a., compounded annually. Contributions are paid on 1st of January each year. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Zoya decides to invest in the fund for the next 20 years. Show that the final value of her investment is given by
$$A_{20}=\frac{12000\times1.09\times(1.09^{20}-1)}{0.09}.$$

answer.worked:
Using the geometric-series result from part (a):
$$\begin{aligned}A_{20}&=\frac{12000(1.09)(1.09^{20}-1)}{0.09}\\A_{20}&\approx\$669\,174.36.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: By how much does this exceed the total contributions Zoya made?

children.label: d
children.prompt:
The company agrees to let Zoya make a higher contribution to the scheme. Let this instalment be $M$. Show that in this case
$$A_{20}=\frac{M\times1.09\times(1.09^{20}-1)}{0.09}.$$

answer.worked:
If the annual contribution is $M$, the value at the end of the 20th year is
$$A_{20}=M(1.09)^{20}+M(1.09)^{19}+\cdots+M(1.09).$$
This is a geometric series with first term $a=M(1.09)$, common ratio $r=1.09$ and $n=20$.
$$\begin{aligned}A_{20}&=\frac{M(1.09)(1.09^{20}-1)}{1.09-1}\\A_{20}&=\frac{M(1.09)(1.09^{20}-1)}{0.09}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: What would Zoya’s annual contribution have to be in order for her superannuation to have a total value of $\$1\,000\,000$ at the end of the 20 years?

answer.worked:
Using the geometric-series result from part (d):
$$\begin{aligned}1000000&=\frac{M(1.09)(1.09^{20}-1)}{0.09}\\M&=\frac{1000000(0.09)}{1.09(1.09^{20}-1)}\\M&\approx\$17\,932.55.\end{aligned}$$
The annual contribution is $\$17\,932.55$.
